The Toybox Pack DLC and Update 8 will be available for Planet Coaster 2 on all platforms on December 4th.

Open your Arts & Crafts kit to create a sprawling city using wooden blocks, paintbrushes and anything you can find in your toybox, as you bring your park to life with the brand-new Toybox Pack. With new scenery, architecture, and a new entertainer, take your creativity to the max! Your guests will also get to enjoy FIVE new attractions, including the Vector - New-Gen Inverting Suspended Coaster and the F&N Thriller - Kid Coaster.

Update 8 includes the return of the Planet Coaster Festive Theme, which has been given a fresh coat of paint and 'holiday cheer' just in time for the festive season. We've also introduced several new weather options, introducing new challenges for your parks, such as plummeting temperatures that can freeze over your pools, and thunderstorms which put your rides at risk. A selection of scenery blueprints from each theme in the original base game, improvements to Management areas across Rides, Utilities and Guests plus Scalable Animatronics are all coming in this update too.

New Weather Features & Improvements
Weather is getting a series of improvements and two new weather states in Update 8
New Seasonal Weather – Snow
Snow will now fall in Temperate and Taiga biomes and settle on surfaces in your park.
A new Guest Need has been added to the game: Warmth.
In cold conditions guests will have a preference for hot food and drinks, prefer indoor dining and covered benches and become uncomfortable if they are too cold for too long.
Park Managers will be able to keep their guests warm by adding the new Electrical Heaters scenery objects.
Sheltered areas will maintain a level of warmth.
Park Managers will need to not only keep their parks warm with Heaters but also their Pools to avoid the water freezing over in colder temperatures.
Pool Heaters can be added to pools to keep them at the right temperature for your guests. Guests will not enter pools that are too cold or frozen.
Park Managers can choose to keep their pools open and warm enough for guests to brave, or close them off during cold snaps to conserve energy and funds.
New Heatmaps have been added to show temperatures in the park.
New Seasonal Weather – Thunderstorms
Thunderstorms are also coming to the game and can appear in all biomes, with an increased chance in a Tropical environment.
Lightning can strike rides, generators and water pumps causing them to breakdown.
Guests will enter a state of panic if their ride is struck by lightning.
Park Managers will need to consider closing particular rides during thunderstorms due to potential lightning strikes.
Heatmap Changes
A new Shade heatmap has been added to the Scenery Heatmaps category.
This heatmap will highlight areas of shade that protect against direct sunlight as well as rain and snow.
A new Temperature heatmap has been added to the Scenery Heatmaps category.
This heatmap will show park temperature in addition to highlighting heated areas, heated Pools and enclosed areas of warmth.
A new Warmth heatmap has been added to the Guest Experience heatmaps category.
This heatmap will indicate individual guests temperatures.
A new Dryness heatmap has been added to the Guest Experience heatmaps category.
This heatmap tracks the dryness needs that are influenced by Weather.
Guests who are in swimwear, in a pool, using a flume or the Wavesim will not be affected by these needs.
The Sunburn heatmap from the Guest Experience category has been reworked and is now the Sun Cream heatmap.
This heatmap will now show each guests exposure to direct sunlight and highlight guest services where they can purchase Sun Cream.
The Needs Cleaning heatmap has been moved from the Scenery category to the Operations category.
Notifications
Frequency of guest ailment state reports has been increased.
New informational reports to inform Park Managers of how to cater to Guests ailments will now appear, for example:
Rain: In rain, guests will prefer dining areas that are sheltered, and may choose to buy umbrellas to keep themselves dry.
Thunderstorms: Guest will leave pools, and some rides/generators could be hit by lightning which could cause your guests to panic.
Sunburn Improvements
Guests suncream no longer lasts forever and can now run out. Guests will now buy more suncream as they try to prevent sunburn.
Hot & Cold Drink Preferences
Guests now have preferences for Hot & Cold food and drinks, depending on weather conditions.
Weather Affects On Utilities
The effectiveness of Solar Panels will now depend on weather conditions and how much sunlight they are exposed to.
Solar Panels in clear sunny conditions will work at 100% efficiency.
Solar Panels in overcast or rainy conditions will have their efficiency noticeably reduced.
Park Managers will need to make sure that Solar Panels are placed in direct sunlight in order for them to generate electricity.
Solar Panels obscured from sunlight, such as placed indoors, beneath a shelter, or in a shaded area will not work.
New notifications will be displayed if a Solar Panel stops working due to one of the above factors.
New Park Settings
Park Managers will now have control over the following game aspects in Sandbox Mode:
The ability to toggle off particular weather conditions entirely.
Adjust sim effects from weather conditions, such as guests getting wet, rides breaking down during storms, pools freezing in cold weather conditions.
Turning off world temperature effects now also influences guests needs for Hot & Cold food and drink, and need for heat sources in cold weather.
Turn off Utilities being affected by weather conditions.
Turn off Pool temperatures.
Scalable Animatronics
The scale of all Animatronic props can now by customised to further fit your creative desires.
Moving Platforms
A new moving platform has been added - Moving Platform Spring
Management & Economy Improvements
Changes to Scenery and Ride Prestige
The area of effect of all scenery has been revised slightly to help reduce large spikes or drops in guest moods. All scenery now has an increased radius of effect and decreased strength.
Prestige for Flat Rides has been rebalanced to prevent unexpectedly high prestige scores when adding multiple extra ride sequences.
To prevent all rides from reaching maximum prestige too easily the maximum prestige bonus a ride can gain is now limited based on its ride type.
This will also create more of a distinction in prestige scores between flat rides and rollercoasters.
Changes to Wear Rates & Upkeep Costs
Servicing rides, power generators and water pumps will now come at a cost, as well as now repairing the ride's condition to 80%.
Rides, power generators and water pumps can still be refurbished to full condition but at an increased cost.
Service badges on rides, power generators and water pumps will no longer prevent condition deterioration but will slow down wear rate, creating a greater challenge when maintaining ride condition.
The wear rates of all rides, power generators and water pumps have been balanced to account for the above in addition to open rides with no guests now receiving less wear.
A rides maintenance tab will now indicate low, average or high wear rate.
Changes to Ride Ticket Pricing
The cost of ride tickets has been rebalanced to offset the changes to upkeep costs.
This will have no effect on players setting custom ride prices.
An improved breakdown of a ride's ticket cost can now be found in a ride's info panel from the ticket cost tooltip.
Improvements to Guest Needs & Thoughts
Guests will now look to leave a pool if they have a pressing need, such as thirst/hunger etc.
A delay has been added to guest needs when in queues, pools and rides to reduce guests needs from dropping too low if they are unable to leave an attraction to satisfy a need.
Changes to Power & Water Utilities
Power/Water capacity and total upkeep has been added to object browser tooltips to aid player decision making when selecting what type of utilities to use.
Cost per unit has also been added to the power generator's object browser tooltip.
The amount of regional power provided by park entrance gates has been reduced from 120 to 60 to provide more challenge to early stages of the game.
Preplaced park entrances will now have each of their power connection nodes connected together by default.
Info panels for power generators & water pumps now display condition penalty and effective capacity data to allow for better power/water management.
Utilities heatmaps now fully highlight rides and flumes.
Existing Ride Upgrades

New Guest Moods from Rides & Queues
Guests can now experience more moods when exiting or queuing for a ride.
When in a queue for a ride guests can now also be Excited or Happy based on the rides prestige.
If the queue for a ride is too long guest's moods will now become Bored or Unhappy based on how long they've been in the queue.
Guests will now become unhappy if they are kicked off of a ride.
After leaving a ride that guests enjoyed, they will have a brief period of grace where they will not register some uncomfortable mood triggers.

Alongside this DLC launch, we've also released Update 7. This FREE update is available to all Planet Coaster 2 players across all platforms.
Update 7 includes a number of new features as well as bug fixes and improvements.

Test your ability to run a successful theme park in this brand-new game mode. Choose from sandbox biomes or career sandbox templates as a starting point and complete challenges to gain cash rewards and continue levelling up your park.
You'll even be able to convert your challenge park into a sandbox park, so you can continue building, customising and improving your dream theme park!
We've implemented a new 3-axis grid system, so you can now rotate buildings on all three axis and add some really unique touches to your park!

It's time to introduce a new way to entertain your guests! Get ready to create awesome arcades in your parks, complete with a selection of classic Atari® arcade machines! Update 9 for Planet Coaster 2 will be available free on all platforms on April 30th.

This update will also bring Planet Coaster 2 support to the ASUS ROG Ally / ROG Xbox Ally!

A new Entertainment tab has been added to the browser.

Included in Update 9 are 14 brand new Arcade Machines and a Prize Counter for guests to enjoy!
Guests can win prizes from the machines directly or tickets which can be swapped for prizes at the Prize Counter.
Park Managers can decide how many tickets and prizes their guests can win from their arcades.
All Arcade Machines with the exception of the Atari machines, will come with colour customisation, allowing you to better tailor them to the theme of your park.

Enhanced flume behaviours

Please note that existing flumes will need to turn the ‘Enhanced Guest Flume Behaviours' toggle on to see the new flume behaviours. Existing flumes in your parks may also be affected visually due to clipping with the new round bottomed flumes - adjustments to your flume placement will resolve this.
Newly placed flumes will use the new flume behaviours toggle by default.
As part of Update 3, all flumes bottoms are now rounded, and inflatables will deform to match this shape as they slide down!

Your guests will also enjoy a number of new ways to travel down the flume special pieces. Depending on their entry speed onto the piece, there will be different directions their raft could take! You will need to toggle ‘Enhanced Guest Flume Behaviours’ on to see this.

Flume jettisoning will also be making its way to the game, with guests reacting to it. Although Jettison looks fun, guests might have a different opinion as they go through the experience and there will be negative reactions from it if they don’t land in water. Panic will overwhelm your guest, and they will leave the park.
On top of the above, we will be making further enhancements to physics and guests behaviours.

Hayo Park Managers!

Last week we were blown away with some of your wonderful creations and you continue to amaze us – see the video below! We also announced that we were working on an update for December. We want to give you an update on its progress and announce Hotfix 2 coming this week on Thursday Nov 21!
Guest Flume Use
Guests will be less likely to change their mind on their way to use a flume
The chance that guests will use flumes to enter a pool has been increased
The weighting of flume prestige within guest decision-making has been increased
The chance of guests riding the same flume multiple times has been increased
Guests will now find full pools less desirable
Guest Queuing Behaviour
Guests will now tolerate longer queues (within reason) and will use more of the available queue path
Queue times being reported by platforms with multiple slides attached will now display accurately
Note: These changes will only affect new guests as they arrive in your parks and will not affect existing guests.
Here’s an update on what the team are working on for the December update, items in bold are new additions or now confirmed from the working on list:
CONFIRMED
UI Enhancements
Edge scrolling for PC.
Browser tabs will remain on-screen whilst in tools menus
Colour picker adjustments:
Exiting the colour picker will apply the setting as well as clicking ‘Confirm’
The input field will no longer require the # when adding manual colours
Correct the mouse failing to move the cursor whilst outside the gradient square
Improve areas where scenery should remember the last custom colour picked

Improved UI responsiveness

For PC players, Angle Snap and other sliders that have an Off option will have functionality for easy toggling
Embedding the create custom ride/coaster UI into the object browser rather than having its own bespoke UI
Added custom rebindable controls for camera tilt and mouse controls

Adding the ability to have separate loading and unloading stations where applicable
Customisable tracked and transport rides

We’ve been thrilled with some of the creations we’ve seen already – take a look at the video below – and much like you, we’re just getting started! Last week we mentioned future updates, and today we wanted to share some highlights of what's coming in our next free update, arriving in December.
Here’s what the team are working on for the next free update in December:
Edge scrolling
Browser tabs will remain on-screen whilst in tools menus
Colour picker adjustments:
Exiting the colour picker will apply the setting as well as clicking ‘Confirm’
The input field will no longer require the # when adding manual colours

Adding the ability to have separate loading and unloading stations where applicable
Adding a new heatmap for Guest Tolerance which will show their tolerance for Fear, Nausea and Ride Height amongst other factors
Adding scenery pieces to create custom coaster supports
Add a selection of glass pieces for players to use in their parks
Adding the ability to change weather in Sandbox
Water droplets will now be visible on the game camera when the camera goes into pools
Increase the possible maximum guest cap whilst playing in solo play in Sandbox Mode
Coaster bug fixes
Correcting jittering special pieces
General stability and performance fixes
In addition to the above we’re also working hard to bring the following additions and enhancements to this update and will update you on our progress in the coming weeks.
Improvements to flume physics behaviour
More realistic guests/dummy behaviours
Allowing multiple guests on flumes at the same time
Adjusted Colourblind friendly heat maps to make them more user friendly
Additional UI enhancements
Streamlined multi-select, Shift/Ctrl will now toggle between options rather than needing to hold the Shift key
Added custom rebindable controls for camera tilt and mouse controls
Customisable tracked and transport rides
Additional guest and staff balancing- Including balancing guest tolerance for queue lengths.
Remove the download limit
